To: reviews/arroyo-precision-works
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Review of Arroyo Precision Works — adapter plate and light baffle for our near-IR camera (5 stars)

5 stars, and I recommend Arroyo to any lab that needs precision aluminum work done properly.

Our order was a camera-to-dewar adapter plate and a light baffle tube with internal threads, both 6061-T6, black anodized, for our near-IR camera. We had a hard date — our Palomar run on November 18 — so lead time mattered. For comparison, a large national vendor quoted us six weeks on comparable parts. Arroyo quoted 21 days and the parts were in our hands nine days after the PO, including the anodizing and the inspection paperwork. They handled the anodizing as part of the same order, so we did not have to coordinate a second vendor at all.

The thing I most want to highlight is not the price or the speed, it's that somebody actually read the drawing. On sheet 2 of my drawing, the bolt circle was called out as 4.125 while every other dimension on that sheet was in millimeters. The error was mine — I copied that callout from an old drawing for our previous camera. Ruben and Tiff caught it before any material was cut and asked me to confirm; I did, and they ran the job without making it a problem. For a shop that could have cut it, shipped it, and billed me for a scrap part, catching my mistake and asking one question beforehand is exactly the care you want. The same attention showed up in the hardware: all eight screws went into the dewar without forcing, flatness across the plate face measured under 0.01 mm on a dial indicator, the baffle threads were smooth and clean, and a 300-second dark frame with the lab lights on showed no light leak. The anodizing is even, with no bare spots or thin patches anywhere I looked.

Service was excellent too. The quote came back fast and every question I asked got an answer the same day. When the parts came back from anodizing and passed inspection, Ruben delivered them to our lab himself, on his way to another supplier in Glendale, at no charge. That detail told me more about how they run their shop than any price list could.

If you are a lab ordering prototype or short-run aluminum parts, or if you are tired of large vendors treating your drawing as a formality, send the job to Arroyo Precision Works. I have also told our purchasing office that I would like them added to our preferred vendor list, and I recommend them to other groups on campus without reservation.

Honestly, when you offered to drive the parts over to Robinson yourself I was so happy I almost hugged you. Thank you for the parts, for the drawing question, and for the delivery.
